email.body1:
Allison, reaching out because SureCost sells procurement intelligence across health systems, ambulatory networks, and retail pharmacy, a wide market for a lean BDR team to cover.

That breadth usually means more in-market accounts than your reps can research and chase, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for SureCost off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Allison, quick follow-up for SureCost.

With a small BDR team across several pharmacy segments, most groups cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit target this quarter. So the gap shows up late, and the quarter becomes a scramble to recover.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings SureCost needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Allison, last bit of proof for SureCost.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how SureCost's reply rate likely compares to other healthcare-software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Allison, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything, and I know running a lean BDR team across several segments keeps you busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to SureCost either way.
